products.name: Pioneer
products.priceBasis: Free design files ≠ a free camera. Lens, printing, magnets, fasteners and light seals extra; no verified kit or assembled offer.
products.shooting: Simple daylight shooting · estimate distance, turn the lens, flick the shutter; wind by the red frame window.
products.build: DIY only verified · print, glue, fit magnets and light seals, then test focus and leaks.
products.openness: Published body + shutter + winding parts and build guide. Bought glass lens and commodity hardware.
products.availability: Files available; no assembled or kit offer verified
products.verdict: Simple controls, but not automatic exposure
products.imageAlt: Physical Pioneer 3D-printed film camera with lens and winding knobs

images.alt: Physical Pioneer 3D-printed film camera with lens and winding knobs

products.imageNote: Physical project photograph from Hackaday’s 2025 release report. One verified camera photograph; no product-store gallery. No generated imagery.

facts.Shooting: Simple box-camera workflow once properly built. Scale/estimated-distance focus, fixed-style magnetic shutter, manual advance using the red window. Not autofocus or metered auto exposure; suitable light and film choice still matter.
facts.Build effort: Substantial hands-on assembly: print body and mechanism, epoxy lens/magnets, make light seals and fit winding parts. Verify shutter, focus and light-tightness before fresh film.
facts.Required parts: Creator’s current guide specifies Thorlabs LA1134 60mm lens, magnets, screws/nuts, foam, elastic and adhesives. No priced complete BOM or current ready-made offer verified.
facts.Running costs: Buy 120 film and pay for development/scans (or process it yourself). Current combined film + lab cost not verified; do not assume cheaper per shot than 35mm.
facts.Evidence limit: The creator’s 2023 shooting report used an older 65mm lens. Released 2025 build uses 60mm; do not transfer that prototype’s exact shutter speed or aperture as a calibrated specification.
facts.Why included: A simple real film design with released body AND shutter files, not a pinhole or a manual large-format system. Easy controls do not mean easy assembly or exposure in any light.

products.attribution: Design files and guide verified; ease judgment is based on controls, not hands-on testing.

sources.title: BFC: what its installed OpenSX70 board does
sources.note: Every SX-70 sold now includes a replacement board. Automatic exposure; Sonar autofocus. Six-month warranty. BFC’s supplied revision is not independently matched to an upstream CAD revision.

sources.title: openSX70: released PCB schematics and board layouts
sources.note: Inspected .sch/.brd files, including MEROE and Sonar designs. These are replacement electronics, not plans for the proprietary Polaroid body, optics or film mechanism.

sources.title: openSX70: operating modes
sources.note: Documents automatic exposure with no dongle, and A100/A600 modes. This newer guide supersedes the 2018 experimental manual that lacked auto exposure.

sources.title: Pioneer: released camera parts
sources.note: Verified 16 STL listings, including body, shutter blade/block and lens barrel. Downloaded and checked the binary bottom-body STL, not just an announcement.

sources.title: Pioneer: creator’s parts list and build guide
sources.note: Current guide specifies a Thorlabs LA1134 60mm singlet, magnetic shutter, rotating focus barrel, hand winding and red-window frame reading. Printing, epoxy, magnets, foam light seals and calibration are builder work.

sources.title: Pioneer predecessor: creator’s shooting report
sources.note: Creator shot two rolls of HP5 Plus. Simple magnetic shutter; older 65mm prototype lens is NOT the 60mm lens specified by the released build.

historicalReferences.name: EZCam
historicalReferences.price: Current complete cost unknown; historical 2025 BOM $108.05
historicalReferences.note: Instax Mini; released six STL parts, wiring and servo firmware. The $108.05 included a 20-shot film pack but excluded filament and salvaged items. The shutter stays open while the button is held: no automatic exposure timing. Creator reports most results were not great. Retained as a prototype reference, not an easy-shoot recommendation.

historicalReferences.name: Pathfinder + LomoGraflok
historicalReferences.price: Complete cost unknown · donor + back + printed parts
historicalReferences.note: Instax Wide; published adapter files, not a complete open camera. Requires drilling rivets and recalibrating focus/rangefinder during conversion. Shooting still needs manual focus, exposure and shutter handling. Excluded for shooting workflow, independently of build difficulty.

historicalReferences.name: IDENTIDEM MRF2
historicalReferences.price: £500 assembled body only · complete cost unknown
historicalReferences.note: Current GB/GBP offer, both red/green grip variants available; replaces the earlier £700 figure. Separate localized browser showed US$681, not an exchange-rate estimate. Required Mamiya Press lens costs extra. Repo’s roughly $300 DIY estimate also does not include the taking lens, labor, shipping or tax. 120 and 35mm panoramas. Body CAD, print files, PCBs and firmware are public; lens is proprietary. LiDAR guides manual focus and the meter SUGGESTS shutter speed: this is not autofocus or automatic exposure. Excluded from easy-shoot shortlist.

historicalReferences.name: PolaPi-Zero
historicalReferences.note: Earlier search result only. Raspberry Pi digital capture and thermal receipt-paper printing, not chemical instant film. Published software/drawings do not make it a film camera.

evidenceNote: “Open” here means useful hardware files or build plans are published, regardless of license. Partial designs are labeled. This is a bounded verified shortlist, not an exhaustive survey. No cheap assembled conventional-film camera passed both the published-design and easy-shoot gates in this review.
caveat: No easy 35mm option was verified: Chromium still lists rewind jams, electrical noise and unfinished auto exposure; OpenCamera lacks repeatable frame advance; Alpha35 has only a README. Manual medium/large-format designs and pinholes were not added just to fill the grid. Pioneer is 120 film, not 35mm. Prices exclude shipping, tax and film unless explicitly stated.
